1	\chapter{Auslander--Buchsbaum}
     2	\label{chap:Albanese_AuslanderBuchsbaum}
     3	% archon:covers AlgebraicJacobian/Albanese/AuslanderBuchsbaum.lean
     4	
     5	
     6	\section{Setup and motivation}
     7	\label{sec:ab_setup}
     8	
     9	A regular projective surface \(S\) over a field --- such as \(\mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1\)
    10	or the product \(C \times C\) of a smooth projective curve \(C\) with itself --- has a regular
    11	local ring at every (closed) point, of Krull dimension \(2\). To extend a rational map
    12	\(f : S \dashrightarrow A\) from \(S\) to an abelian variety across a codimension-\(2\) closed
    13	point, one argues that the local ring \(\mathcal{O}_{S,x}\) at such a point has \emph{depth at
    14	least} \(2\), hence a rational function with no codimension-\(1\) poles on a neighbourhood of \(x\)
    15	extends across \(x\). The depth \(\geq 2\) inequality is exactly what the
    16	Auslander--Buchsbaum formula gives: for a regular local ring \(R\) one has \(\text{pd}_R(R) = 0\),
    17	so
    18	\[
    19	  \text{depth}(R) \;=\; \text{pd}_R(R) + \text{depth}(R) \;=\; \text{depth}(R)
    20	\]
    21	trivially, but combined with the regular-sequence definition of depth and the fact that a
    22	regular local ring of dimension \(d\) admits an \(R\)-regular sequence of length \(d\) generating
    23	the maximal ideal, one obtains \(\text{depth}(R) = \dim(R)\), i.e.\ \(R\) is Cohen--Macaulay
    24	(\cref{cor:regular_cohen_macaulay} below). This is the input A.4.a needs.
    25	
    26	This chapter packages:
    27	\begin{enumerate}
    28	  \item the regular-sequence definition of depth and its \(\text{Ext}\) reformulation
    29	    (\cref{def:depth} and \cref{lem:depth_via_ext}),
    30	  \item the projective-dimension invariant of a finitely-generated module
    31	    (\cref{def:projective_dimension}),
    32	  \item the depth-on-a-short-exact-sequence lemma
    33	    (\cref{lem:depth_short_exact_sequence}),
    34	  \item the Auslander--Buchsbaum formula proper
    35	    (\cref{thm:auslander_buchsbaum}), and
    36	  \item the corollary regular \(\Rightarrow\) Cohen--Macaulay
    37	    (\cref{cor:regular_cohen_macaulay}).
    38	\end{enumerate}
    39	A short closing paragraph (\cref{sec:ab_application_to_a4a}) explains how A.4.a
    40	consumes \cref{cor:regular_cohen_macaulay} to push a codim-1 extension across a
    41	codim-2 point.
    42	
    43	\section{Depth of a module over a local ring}
    44	\label{sec:ab_depth}
    45	
    46	\begin{definition}
    47	
    48	\leanok
    49	  [Depth of a module]
    50	  \label{def:depth}
    51	  \lean{RingTheory.Module.depth}
    52	  \textit{Source: [Stacks Project], tag 00LF (definition-depth).}
    53	  Let \(R\) be a commutative ring, let \(I \subseteq R\) be an ideal, and let \(M\) be a finitely
    54	  generated \(R\)-module. The \emph{\(I\)-depth} of \(M\), written \(\text{depth}_I(M)\), is the
    55	  supremum in \(\{0, 1, 2, \dots, \infty\}\) of the lengths of \(M\)-regular sequences contained

body: 'Milne 3.1/3.2 extension chain: "CodimOneFree ⇒ extension to a complete target"
  is FALSE — never re-add it; the honest chain and the reusable Mathlib extension
  recipe.


  - **Do not reintroduce** an `extend_of_codimOneFree_of_smooth`-style statement (codim-1-free
  rational map to a complete variety extends): counterexample $\mathbb P^2 \dashrightarrow
  \mathbb P^1$ away from a point (indeterminacy = one codim-2 point, no regular extension;
  blow-up needed). Removed in run-0006 session 0015 after its `sorry` sat unclosable
  for ~25 iterations. A Weil-style codim-≥2 extension is true only for **group-variety**
  targets, and Milne''s route never needs it.

  - **Honest chain** (all in `Albanese/CodimOneExtension.lean` + `Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean`):
  Milne 3.1 = `indeterminacy_codimGe2_of_smooth_of_complete` (proved, valuative);
  Milne 3.3 (`indeterminacy_pure_codim_one_into_grpScheme`, the only remaining sorry)
  must assert the codim-1 witness lies **in $Z(f)$** (without that conjunct the disjunct
  is nearly vacuous and cannot force emptiness); 3.3 + 3.1 ⇒ $Z(f)=\emptyset$ (`av_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty`);
  then extension. **Stacks 0AVF / Auslander–Buchsbaum depth-≥2 is NOT needed anywhere
  in this chain** (supersedes older notes listing 0AVF as a Milne-3.1 blocker).

  - **Recipe: extension from empty indeterminacy** (`existsUnique_hom_of_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty`,
  reduced X / separated Y): witness `X.topIso.inv ≫ X.homOfLE hdom.ge ≫ f.toPartialMap.hom`
  where `hdom : f.toPartialMap.domain = ⊤` (`toPartialMap.domain = f.domain` is `rfl`);
  rational-class equality via `PartialMap.toRationalMap_eq_iff.mpr ⟨⊤, …⟩` + `simp
  only [PartialMap.restrict_hom, Scheme.Hom.toPartialMap, Scheme.topIso_hom, Scheme.ι_toIso_inv_assoc,
  Scheme.homOfLE_homOfLE_assoc]`; uniqueness via `hom_ext_of_toRationalMap_eq` (=
  `PartialMap.toRationalMap_eq_iff.mp` + `Opens.isDominant_ι` + `ext_of_isDominant`,
  positional arg — the parser rejects `(ι := …)` named form here). Both lemmas need
  `set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false` BEFORE the docstring (`(restrict
  …).domain` / `Hom.toPartialMap` defeq walls).

  - **Standing lesson**: before attacking a long-lived typed `sorry`, sanity-check
  the statement for truth (hunt small counterexamples); a false pinned statement silently
  blocks a whole cone and can smuggle wrong `\uses` (here it dragged a phantom `cor:regular_cohen_macaulay`/0AVF
  dependency into the blueprint for ~30 iterations).'

 \section{Setup and motivation}
 \label{sec:ab_setup}
 
-A regular projective surface \(S\) over a field --- such as \(\mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1\)
-or the product \(C \times C\) of a smooth projective curve \(C\) with itself --- has a regular
-local ring at every (closed) point, of Krull dimension \(2\). To extend a rational map
-\(f : S \dashrightarrow A\) from \(S\) to an abelian variety across a codimension-\(2\) closed
-point, one argues that the local ring \(\mathcal{O}_{S,x}\) at such a point has \emph{depth at
-least} \(2\), hence a rational function with no codimension-\(1\) poles on a neighbourhood of \(x\)
-extends across \(x\). The depth \(\geq 2\) inequality is exactly what the
-Auslander--Buchsbaum formula gives: for a regular local ring \(R\) one has \(\text{pd}_R(R) = 0\),
-so
-\[
-  \text{depth}(R) \;=\; \text{pd}_R(R) + \text{depth}(R) \;=\; \text{depth}(R)
-\]
-trivially, but combined with the regular-sequence definition of depth and the fact that a
-regular local ring of dimension \(d\) admits an \(R\)-regular sequence of length \(d\) generating
-the maximal ideal, one obtains \(\text{depth}(R) = \dim(R)\), i.e.\ \(R\) is Cohen--Macaulay
-(\cref{cor:regular_cohen_macaulay} below). This is the input A.4.a needs.
+The Auslander--Buchsbaum formula relates the projective dimension of a finite module over a
+Noetherian local ring to its depth.  For a regular local ring, a regular system of parameters also
